metadata.title: Spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking by hydromagnetic buoyancy
metadata.authors: Piyali Chatterjee, Dhrubaditya Mitra, Axel Brandenburg, Matthias Rheinhardt

nodes.name: Stratified Cartesian slab with embedded magnetic layer
nodes.statement: A Cartesian slab of ideal gas, stably stratified along $z$, contains a narrow horizontal magnetic layer of thickness $H_B$ in magnetostatic equilibrium: a fraction of the gas pressure is replaced by magnetic pressure and the temperature is reduced so the density is unchanged, leaving the layer initially non-buoyant.
nodes.statement_clean: An ideal-gas slab stratified in z with a thin embedded magnetic layer in magnetostatic equilibrium.

nodes.name: Alfvén speed $v_{A0}$ and Alfvén time $t_{A0}$
nodes.statement: $v_{\rm A0} = B_0/\sqrt{\rho_0\mu_0}$ is the Alfvén speed for the initial $y$-directed field of strength $B_0$, with $\rho_0$ the bottom density and $\mu_0$ the vacuum permeability; the Alfvén time is $t_{\rm A0} = L_y/v_{\rm A0}$.

nodes.name: Mean fields and fluctuations under horizontal averaging
nodes.statement: Overbars denote $xy$-averaging, so $\meanBB = \meanBB(z,t)$ and $\meanUU = \meanUU(z,t)$. Velocity and field fluctuations are $\uu = \UU - \meanUU$ and $\bb = \BB - \meanBB$; with no imposed field, $\meanB_z = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Define mean fields by horizontal averaging and split B and U into mean plus fluctuation.

nodes.name: Mean electromotive force $\meanEMF = \overline{\uu\times\bb}$
nodes.statement: The mean EMF is the cross-correlation $\meanEMF = \overline{\uu\times\bb}$ of the velocity and magnetic fluctuations after horizontal averaging.

nodes.name: $\alpha$-effect kernel and turbulent diffusion kernel
nodes.statement: In the constitutive relation for $\meanEMF$, $\alpha_{ij}$ is a pseudo-tensor whose symmetric part produces the $\alpha$ effect, and $\eta_{ij}$ is a true tensor whose symmetric part describes turbulent diffusion.

nodes.name: Test-field Fourier kernels $\hat{\alpha}_{ij}(z,k)$, $\hat{\eta}_{ij}(z,k)$
nodes.statement: The convolution kernels in $z$ become $z$-dependent multipliers $\hat{\alpha}_{ij}(z,k)$ and $\hat{\eta}_{ij}(z,k)$ in Fourier space and are computed by the test-field method; only the $k = \pi/L_z$ constituent is retained, and the $k$ argument is suppressed.

nodes.name: Run pairs A$\pm$ and B$\pm$
nodes.statement: Two pairs of runs A$\pm$ and B$\pm$ are defined; within each pair the initial velocities are exact mirror images about a vertical plane and so carry opposite initial kinetic helicities. Pair A also contains random vertical motions of Mach number $\sim 10^{-5}$ (initial $\bra{\ww\cdot\uu}/\urms w_{\rm rms} \approx 2\times 10^{-5}$); pair B has none, leaving only numerical noise ($\approx 4\times 10^{-10}$).

nodes.name: Constitutive relation for $\meanEMF$ (Eq. 1)
nodes.statement: $(\overline{\uu\times\bb})_i = \alpha_{ij}\circ \meanB_j - \eta_{ij}\circ \meanJ_j$, where $\circ$ denotes spatial convolution.

nodes.name: Reflectional symmetries of the base state
nodes.statement: Reflections at planes $z=\const$ change the system because of the stratification; reflections at planes $y=\const$ leave it invariant; reflections at planes $x=\const$ are equivalent to flipping the sign of the initial field of the magnetic layer.

nodes.name: Paired helical eigenmodes with equal growth rates
nodes.statement: If the linearized system admits helical eigenmodes, they occur in pairs with opposite helicities and identical growth (or decay) rates; analogous pairing holds for any stable quasi-stationary helical solutions of the nonlinear system.
conclusions: Helical linear eigenmodes appear in $\pm$ helicity pairs with the same growth rate
Stable helical nonlinear solutions, if any, also appear in $\pm$ helicity pairs

nodes.name: Exponential amplification of helicity from sign-imbalanced initial conditions
nodes.statement: Depending on the sign of the slight imbalance in net kinetic helicity in the initial perturbation, the kinetic and current helicities are exponentially amplified during the linear stage of the instability with the same growth rate but opposite signs.
assumptions: Initial velocity perturbation carries a slight random net kinetic helicity
Linear (early) stage of the magnetic buoyancy instability
conclusions: Kinetic and current helicities grow exponentially
Sign of the amplified helicity is set by the sign of the initial imbalance

nodes.name: Sign-flip symmetry of $\hat{\alpha}_{yy}$ within a run pair
nodes.statement: Within each pair, the $\hat{\alpha}_{yy}(z,t)$ map of the negative-helicity run is, to good accuracy, the sign-inverse of that of the positive-helicity run.
assumptions: Runs A$+$ and A$-$ initialised as exact mirror images
Mean EMF decomposition (DP288.5) and Fourier kernel (DP288.6) hold

nodes.name: $\hat{\alpha}_{xx}$ has spatially uniform sign at each time
nodes.statement: $\hat{\alpha}_{xx}$ is found to keep the same sign throughout the entire domain at each instant, so its spatial average $\bra{\hat{\alpha}_{xx}}(t)$ captures its evolution; unlike $\bra{\ww\cdot\uu}$, the sign of $\bra{\hat{\alpha}_{xx}}$ never changes.
assumptions: Runs A$\pm$, B$\pm$ in the saturated regime
conclusions: $\bra{\hat{\alpha}_{xx}}(t)$ has fixed sign throughout the simulation
By contrast $\bra{\ww\cdot\uu}(t)$ exhibits sign changes (e.g. at $t/t_{\rm A0}\approx 2$)

nodes.name: Final helicity sign may differ from the initial sign
nodes.statement: The asymptotic sign of the helicity need not coincide with the initial one: e.g. run A$+$ starts with positive helicity but ends with negative, undergoing several sign changes in the kinematic stage; volumetrically, this is interpretable as patches of one handedness shrinking in the direction of the curvature vector.
assumptions: Helicity is a volume integral over patches of mixed sign of $\ww\cdot\uu$
conclusions: Sign of the saturated helicity is not determined by the initial sign

nodes.name: Spontaneous $\alpha$ effect without rotation
nodes.statement: The magnetic buoyancy instability amplifies magnetic and velocity fields with either sign of helicity; the selection of one sign during the nonlinear stage produces an $\alpha$ effect under otherwise parity-invariant conditions, providing a mechanism for mean-field generation in the absence of $\OO$ or other a-priori pseudoscalar.
assumptions: No imposed pseudoscalar a-priori beyond the magnetic field itself
conclusions: Net kinetic / current helicity emerges spontaneously
Symmetric part of $\alpha_{ij}$ becomes nonzero, sustaining $\meanBB$

nodes.name: Run pair A$\pm$ (vertical motions present)
nodes.statement: In pair A$\pm$ the initial velocity contains horizontal eddies plus random vertical motions of Mach number $\sim 10^{-5}$, giving initial $\bra{\ww\cdot\uu}/\urms w_{\rm rms}\approx 2\times 10^{-5}$; the two runs share growth rate and saturated energies but acquire opposite helicity signs that emerge after about one Alfvén time.

nodes.name: Run pair B$\pm$ (no initial vertical motions)
nodes.statement: In pair B$\pm$ the vertical motions are set to zero, leaving only numerical noise as the source of helicity ($\approx 4\times 10^{-10}$); the same parity breaking is observed, demonstrating that the effect persists for vanishingly small initial helicity imbalance.

nodes.name: Cold bubbles in galaxy clusters
nodes.statement: Stably stratified, weakly rotating galaxy clusters fit the prerequisites of the mechanism; magnetic and thermal buoyancy effects already invoked to explain cold bubbles in clusters are candidate sites for the spontaneous parity-breaking $\alpha$ effect.

nodes.name: Analogy with biochemical homochirality
nodes.statement: The amplitude equations for two competing helical modes in hydrodynamics share with Frank-type homochirality models the mutual-antagonism term, by which one helicity sign grows at the expense of the other; both also fail to reach a stationary state in closed systems with finite resources.
nodes.origin_citation: Frank 1953; Soai et al. 1995; Plasson & Brandenburg 2010

nodes.name: Comparison with Taylor–Couette and Bénard parity breaking
nodes.statement: Spontaneous parity breaking is known in counter-rotating Taylor–Couette flow (where rotation supplies the axial vector) and in asymmetric square Bénard convection (where roll vorticity does); in the present problem the magnetic field plays the role of the axial vector.

nodes.name: MRI as a candidate for the same parity-breaking class
nodes.statement: The magneto-rotational instability is a plausible second example: with rotation but without stratification or current density there is no a-priori pseudoscalar, so any net helicity it produces would have to come from spontaneous parity breaking.

nodes.name: Nonlinear amplitude equations for the present instability
nodes.statement: Deriving Ginzburg–Landau-type nonlinear amplitude equations for the magnetic-buoyancy parity-breaking instability is left for future work; the existing Fauvé et al. equations for hydrodynamic counterparts are not directly applicable.

nodes.name: Status of the incoherent $\alpha$–shear dynamo
nodes.statement: The incoherent $\alpha$–shear dynamo invokes kinetic helicity fluctuating about zero; the present results suggest revisiting whether a spontaneous parity-breaking instability rather than incoherent fluctuations is responsible for large-scale fields in shear-driven setups.
